document.title: feat(shell): blur the Deck App behind the VitaDeck Shell
document.summary: While the Shell is open, the Deck App canvas renders into a render texture, `src/ui/blur.c` box-downsamples it to 1/16, and the result is stretched back under the Shell. A new `minesweeper-shell` Benchmark Mode scenario measures that frame.
document.why: The Shell was [just transparent](source:s2) over the Deck App, and Máté asked for a blur behind it that does not [incur an unnecessarily large performance cost](source:s2).

sources.label: PR #152
sources.title: feat(shell): blur the Deck App behind the VitaDeck Shell
sources.gist: Blur the Deck App behind the Shell with a downsample chain; Vita3K and host benchmarks show about +0.2 ms CPU per Shell frame.

sources.label: Claude Code session · Nov 5
sources.gist: Add blur behind the VitaDeck Shell (currently just transparent); benchmark to make sure it is not incurring an unnecessarily large performance cost.

lookFor: The request asks to [make sure the cost isn't unnecessarily large](source:s2). On the Vita the blur adds about 4 ms of UI work per Shell frame, with no dropped frames. A frozen-backdrop variant measured cheaper than no blur at all ([PR #152](source:s1)), but it stops Deck App animation behind the Shell, so it is not in this PR.

groups.title: Blur the Deck App behind the Shell
groups.why: The Shell drew only a tint over the Deck App; the [request](source:s2) asks for a blur.
groups.summary: `draw_frame` in `src/main.c` and the smoke harness wrap `bootstrap_draw_deck_canvas` in `blur_begin`/`blur_end` while the Shell is visible, and `src/ui/blur.c` halves the captured canvas four times before stretching the 60×34 level over the screen.

attention.note: With the Shell open, the Vita spends 3.85 ms more wall time per frame in the `shell` span, and UI thread CPU rises from 38% to 48.6%. FPS stays at 59.4 with no dropped frames, but only about 7 ms of slack remains. `draw_frame` re-renders and re-blurs the Deck App every Shell frame so live apps stay live behind the tint; a backdrop frozen when the Shell opens measured 2.5 ms of UI work and 13% CPU.

fileNotes.src/ui/blur.c: Render-texture chain, bilinear and clamped, copied with blending off.
fileNotes.src/main.c: Blurs the canvas only while the Shell is visible.
fileNotes.src/core/bootstrap.c: Unloads the render textures before closing the window.
fileNotes.tests/smoke_harness.c: Draws the Shell screenshot the way `main.c` does.
fileNotes.tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/15-shell-hom: Failure screen text is now blurred behind the Shell.

groups.title: Benchmark the Shell frame
groups.why: The [request](source:s2) asks to benchmark the blur's cost, and no scenario kept the Shell open.
groups.summary: The `shell` flag on `BenchScenario` makes `bench_shell_open` true, and `main.c` presses Start for the Shell whenever that differs from `shell_is_visible`, so `minesweeper-shell` measures the Shell over Minesweeper and later scenarios get it closed.

attention.note: The re-recorded Vita3K baseline moves every scenario, not only `minesweeper-shell`. The PR says the base build shows the same drift on that Mac, so the old numbers no longer described it. The device baseline moves within a few percent and gains `minesweeper-shell`.

fileNotes.src/main.c: Toggles the Shell through System Input to match the scenario.
fileNotes.tests/bench/baselines/vita3k/meta.json: Baseline now from commit 1ad4ccae on the i9 MacBook Pro.
fileNotes.src/core/bench.c: Adds the `shell` field, set on every scenario, and `bench_shell_open`.
fileNotes.tests/bench/baselines/vita/meta.json: Points the device baseline at the blur build, recorded on the Vita.
fileNotes.tests/bench/baselines/vita/result.json: Device numbers for all five scenarios, adding `minesweeper-shell`.

groups.title: Blur the Deck App behind the Shell

before.note: Each Shell frame now costs six render targets (full-size canvas, four 2x downsamples, the screen), each a GXM scene on the Vita. Dropping the upsample chain cut three scenes; the stretched 60×34 level is slightly blockier but sits under the Shell's alpha-200 tint. With the Shell hidden, `draw_frame` takes the old path.

after.note: With the Shell open, the Vita spends 3.85 ms more wall time per frame in the `shell` span, and UI thread CPU rises from 38% to 48.6%. FPS stays at 59.4 with no dropped frames, but only about 7 ms of slack remains. `draw_frame` re-renders and re-blurs the Deck App every Shell frame so live apps stay live behind the tint; a backdrop frozen when the Shell opens measured 2.5 ms of UI work and 13% CPU.

before.note: The re-recorded Vita3K baseline moves every scenario, not only `minesweeper-shell`. The PR says the base build shows the same drift on that Mac, so the old numbers no longer described it. The device baseline has no `minesweeper-shell` entry yet.

after.note: The re-recorded Vita3K baseline moves every scenario, not only `minesweeper-shell`. The PR says the base build shows the same drift on that Mac, so the old numbers no longer described it. The device baseline moves within a few percent and gains `minesweeper-shell`.
